summary: Internal Quenverell training deck (June 2021) introducing bioinformatics to medicinal chemists across the group: what expression and genetic data can and cannot tell a chemistry team, how to read a volcano plot and a pathway table, and how to request an analysis. Not client-facing.

slides.title: Bioinformatics for chemists
slides.subtitle: Internal training | Quenverell Computational Ltd, a Tarnovell company | June 2021

slides.title: Why this session
bullets: Group chemists increasingly receive our target and biomarker readouts
Aim: read them critically and know what to ask
Ninety minutes, no coding

slides.title: Agenda
bullets: What bioinformatics is for in a discovery programme
Expression data in one slide
Reading a volcano plot
Pathways and networks
Genetic evidence
How to request work

slides.title: Where bioinformatics fits in a programme
bullets: Before chemistry: which target, which disease subgroup
During chemistry: what compounds do to cells
Before the clinic: which patients, which markers
Throughout: is the data good enough to decide?

slides.title: What it cannot do
bullets: Replace an assay
Make weak data strong
Give certainty about mechanism from one experiment

slides.title: RNA-seq in one slide
bullets: Count how many RNA copies of each gene a sample contains
Compare disease and control, or treated and untreated
Thousands of genes tested at once, so false positives are expected
Replicates matter more than sequencing depth

slides.title: Reading a volcano plot
bullets: x-axis: size of the change (log fold change)
y-axis: confidence (adjusted p-value)
Top corners: large, confident changes
Ask: how many replicates? which correction?

slides.title: Single-cell data
bullets: Tells you which cell type expresses the target
Useful for safety and tissue questions
Small studies can mislead; check cell numbers

slides.title: Pathway tables
bullets: Groups of genes that act together
Enrichment means more pathway genes changed than chance
Overlapping pathways inflate the story

slides.title: Genetic evidence
bullets: Variants associated with disease point to genes
Strongest when the gene and direction of effect are clear
Combined with expression to rank targets

slides.title: Putting it together: target ranking
bullets: Evidence score per gene across sources
Liabilities flagged: broad expression, paralogs
Output is a ranked short list, not a decision

slides.title: Good questions to ask a bioinformatician
bullets: What data went in and how was it checked?
What would change the ranking?
Which result would you bet on?

slides.title: How to request an analysis
bullets: Raise a request in the shared project tracker
Include the decision you need to make
We reply with scope and timing within a week

slides.title: Glossary
bullets: Differential expression: change in gene activity between conditions
Enrichment: over-representation of a gene set
Batch effect: unwanted variation from processing
Stratification: splitting patients by expected response

slides.title: Exercise
bullets: Read the example target readout in the handout
Write down two questions for the analyst
Discuss in pairs for ten minutes
